summary: Rank–nullity for p ↦ vᴴ·diag(T, −T)·p, v a basis of the link: the map is onto and its kernel is the link.

steps.claim: Let v be a basis matrix of link(γ) (d = dim link(γ) columns, with a left inverse).
Rank–nullity for the linear map p ↦ vᴴ·linkForm·p on E^{2(k+1)}: rank + nullity = 2(k+1).
The map is onto E^d (linkForm = diag(T, −T) is invertible and v has a left inverse, which gives a right inverse), and its kernel is link(γ) (shown next); so d + d = 2(k+1), i.e. d = k+1.
steps.lean:
rw [LinearMap.range_eq_top.2 (⟨S.linkForm⁻¹ *ᵥ ‹_›ᴴ *ᵥ ·, by simp_all [middleGram, det_neg,
          ← conjTranspose_mul]⟩), (_ : LinearMap.ker _ = link γ)] at this; simp_all [← two_mul]

steps.claim: The kernel is link(γ): p is in it iff p is orthogonal for diag(T, −T) to every column of v, i.e. to the whole link, iff p ∈ link(γ) (mem_link_iff_orthogonal).
steps.lean:
ext; rw [mem_link_iff_orthogonal]; simp [← e, star_mulVec_dotProduct]
  simp [star_dotProduct _ (_ *ᵥ _), dotProduct_eq_zero_iff]
